newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast spot products extend strong gains Tues..
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast spot products extend strong gains Tues..

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices jumped early Tuesday as ongoing concerns about supply forced refiners to raise their bids.
The morning rally extended a weeklong climb in prices on the West Coast, returning the region's gasoline prices to premiums over other U.S. areas.
"We're tight on products," a broker said. "There's lots of buyers."
Traders said few barrels were sold early despite the rally, and that no new refinery problems added to the tightening of inventories.
In Los Angeles, CARB regular unleaded gasoline rose about 2.50 to 74.50/75.50, with a deal likely done at 74.75 cents a gallon, traders said.
Prices for West Coast spot products, which reflect what dealers charge at the pipeline, rose 10 percent last week on earlier refinery shutdowns and strong agricultural demand, traders said.
CARB diesel fuel traded between 66.50/67.50 cents, a 1.50-cent rise since Monday in Los Angeles.
Conventional gasoline in L.A. rose roughly 2.00 cents a gallon to 67/69 cents, while jet fuel increased to 61/62 cents amid the increased buying.
The rise in prompt prices of CARB gasoline has returned the grade to a four cent premium over U.S Gulf material, after several weeks of depressed prices.
CARB, which contains fuel additive methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE), generally costs about three to five cents a gallon more to make than gasoline in other regions.
